history.recommendation_text: In paragraph 68 of its report, the Board recommended that the Administration determine the support account share of after-service health insurance expenditure on the basis of actual costs incurred within peacekeeping operations.
history.reference_raw: Recommendations contained in the report of the Board of Auditors for the 12 -month period ended 30 June 2020 (A/75/5 (Vol. II)
history.entities_raw: Department of Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance
history.sg_progress: The General Assembly prescribed pay-as-you-go financing of after-service health insurance, which funds the benefit as it is utilized after staff members retire rather than as the benefit is earned. Determination of the support account share of after-service health insurance based on the actual costs incurred within peacekeeping operations would require the Assembly to approve a change from pay-as-you-go to pay-as-you-accrue financing of after-service health insurance benefits similar to the manner of funding pension benefits. The pay-as-you-go method does not capture costs as incurred during the active career of peacekeeping staff. Under the pay-as-you-go financing method, the total annual cost of after-service health insurance for all enrolled retirees is apportioned to the support account on the basis of the proportion of retirees who incumbered a post funded by peacekeeping operations at retirement compared with the total number of all after-service health insurance participants. This ratio changes over time on the basis of the different rates of retirements of staff on posts funded by peacekeeping operations, the regular budget and extrabudgetary resources. The considerable impact that the recent closure and downsizing of peacekeeping missions has had and will continue to have on separation and retirement rates requires detailed reviews, including external actuarial analyses. Additional review continues to be required during 2026, in consideration of the expected further impact that the recent UN80 Initiative measures will have on the incidence and pattern of projected separations and retirements, the resulting effect on the proportion of total after-service health insurance participants emanating from peacekeeping operations and the related impact on the short-term and longer-term apportionment of after-service health insurance costs. B. Recommendations contained in the report of the Board of Auditors for the 12-month period ended 30 June 2022 (A/77/5 (Vol. II), chap. II)
